paragraphs: The GLE63 AMG has been the flagship performance variant of the GLE-Class range since the GLE nameplate replaced the M-Class in 2015. Across its two generations, it has used two different twin-turbo V8 engines: the earlier W166 generation (2015–2019) uses the 5.5-litre M157, while the current V167 generation (2019–present) uses the 4.0-litre M177 — a smaller but more advanced unit that also appears across the wider Mercedes-AMG range. Both are genuine AMG hand-built engines, and both carry the same specialist rebuild considerations — valve seal wear and coolant system degradation are the key patterns to look for, regardless of which generation you own.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLE63 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the GLE63 AMG from 2015 to 2019 (W166 generation). Known for valve seal and coolant system wear — see the callout above. We replace valve seals and inspect and replace coolant system components as standard on every M157 rebuild.

The current 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, fitted from 2019. A smaller, more advanced unit than the M157, but with a similar wear pattern — valve seal and coolant system wear are the key areas we address on every M177 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLE63 AMG spans two distinct V8 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M157 part will work on an M177 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLE-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
